evidence.baseline: is the part of this work we hold most loosely, and we would rather say so plainly than let the confidence of prose disguise it ... offered in the knowledge that many hands, wiser about governance than ours, will need to redraw much of it ... It is to frame it well enough that better minds than ours take it up.
evidence.shipped: The proposed constitution is a first sketch. ... Real participants, conflicts, jurisdictions, and harms will reveal what the manuscript cannot foresee. ... The design should be marked up before it is revered.

findings.diagnosis: Every claim survives in outline and the first person plural humility is gone, which is the loss that matters here: the volume card assigns the builders' commitments to we, and this is the one section in the part whose entire function is the builders admitting the limit of their own authority. Confidence of prose disguising uncertainty is also precisely the failure the section warns against, so the shipped version's flat declaratives perform the thing the baseline disclaims. The shipped sentence with an idea the baseline lacks, the design should be marked up before it is revered, names reverence as the failure mode; it is quoted here for the author, and the baseline's the sketch is meant to be marked up carries the working half.

evidence.baseline: The enumeration fence, the two-entity design, the specific mechanisms of accountability, the constitutional provisions, and the sketch mark before a set of starting ideas.

findings.diagnosis: The enumeration fence interrupted the subject with a three-item list carrying no verb, so comma pairs would have blurred the boundaries. The syntax was rebuilt: the sentence states what is held most loosely and the colon delivers the enumeration. The sketch mark introduced a specification and became a colon.
